references.text: Pharaoh's earlier command to the midwives to kill male infants at birth, which this verse expands to include the entire people
Moses was placed in a basket on the Nile as a direct result of this command to throw male infants into the river
The Nile, which was used to kill Hebrew children, was later turned into blood as God's judgment against Egypt
The psalm describes how God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate His people, a reference to the persecution under Pharaoh
Stephen's speech refers to this event where Pharaoh acted treacherously toward the Israelites and forced them to expose their infants
Herod's killing of male children in Bethlehem mirrors Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants
Moses' parents hid him in faith and did not fear the king's command, a direct reference to this death sentence
Theological irony: Pharaoh's plan to kill Israelite firstborns turns against him when God takes the Egyptians' firstborn.
Fulfillment of the irony: God's judgment strikes precisely the firstborn sons Pharaoh tried to exterminate.
Direct narrative connection: Moses' rescue is a concrete breach of the decree to throw male infants into the Nile.
